standard_prerequisites: Context span 2424-2436: Y = A^1_k mapping to X = A^1_k/R where R = {(t, t)} union {(t, -t), t != 0}; an immersion Y -> A^n_X over X would be given by regular functions f_1, ..., f_n on Y; the fibre product of Y with the covering A^{n+1}_k -> A^n_X is the scheme {(f_1(t), ..., f_n(t), t)} union {(f_1(t), ..., f_n(t), -t), t != 0} with the obvious morphism to A^{n+1}_k, which is not an immersion
The context closing sentence: this gives a counter example with X quasi-separated

The positive backdrop (section opening, 2402-2406): for schemes, a locally finite type morphism from an affine scheme immerses into some A^n_X (Morphisms, quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S) - provenance only
core_obligations: Y = A^1_k is affine and the structure map Y -> X is of finite type, with X quasi-separated (context)
Any morphism Y -> A^n_X over X is given by n regular functions f_i on Y (context opening of the computation)

The context fibre-product display shows the pullback of such an immersion to the covering A^{n+1}_k is the displayed two-branch scheme whose morphism to A^{n+1}_k is not an immersion; pulling back an immersion along the covering would keep it an immersion, so no immersion Y -> A^n_X over X exists
proof_roadmap: Instantiate Y -> X from the context
Parameterize a would-be immersion by the functions f_i as in the context
Conclude by the context fibre-product computation
